text:
They all gave up fields and houses for Cheng. His elder brothers were furious that he was being overly generous with his favors; they went to his home to humiliate and harass him. Cheng, having spent a long time among the bandits, was accustomed to violence. Hearing this, he flew into a great rage and said, "I have returned, and no one else was willing to provide me with even a single room. Fortunately, my third brother cared for our fraternal bond, yet you now punish and blame him. Do you wish to drive me away?"

He threw a stone at Xiao <note>The name Xiao means Filial Piety</note>. Ren and Yi <note>The names Ren and Yi mean Benevolence and Righteousness</note> each came out with a staff. Cheng grabbed Zhong and Xin <note>The names Zhong and Xin mean Loyalty and Trustworthiness</note> and beat them both countless times. Cheng did not wait for them to sue him; he sued them first. The magistrate again sent someone to consult Youyu <note>The name Youyu means Brotherly Love</note>. Youyu had no choice but to go. He stated that he felt deeply ashamed of being the head of the family and said nothing, only weeping. When pressed for an answer, he only asked the official to provide a fair judgment.

The magistrate then ruled that Xiao and the others must each give up portions of their fields and property to return them to Cheng, so that the seven shares would be equal. From then on, Ren and Yi showed double the affection and respect to Cheng. While talking and laughing, they suddenly touched upon the matter of their mother's burial, and they all wept. Cheng grew determined and said, "To be so unkind as we were is to be no better than beasts." He then wished to open the grave to rebury her properly. Ren and Yi ran to inform Youyu. Youyu hurried home to advise against it, but Cheng would not listen and set a date.

<summary>Cheng violently defends his brother Youyu's generosity against the other brothers, leading to a legal settlement and a plan to rebury their mother.</summary>
<keywords>Pu Songling, Liaozhai Zhiyi, filial piety, inheritance dispute, legal judgment, reburial, fraternal conflict</keywords>
